Hi Olivia / Tom — thanks for the questionnaire — we started filling it out inline and I wanted to call out the key details on KMS/CMK/HSM so you have a clear technical answer for security. Summary below; I've attached a short technical note as well.

Short answers: 
- At-rest: data stored in Redwood is encrypted with AES-256. By default, keys are managed by Redwood KMS.
- Customer-managed keys (CMK): supported. We offer two models: 
  * Hosted CMK (recommended): FinBank provision an AWS KMS CMK in your account and grant Redwood a restricted, time-limited grant to use the key for envelope encryption. Redwood never has access to the unwrapped root key material; we receive wrapped keys for processing.
  * Bring-your-own-HSM: for customers requiring hardware-backed keys, we can integrate with AWS CloudHSM or a supported external HSM via PKCS#11. In this setup, key operations (sign/decrypt) occur in the HSM in your tenant; Redwood services operate against non-extractable keys.
- In-transit: TLS 1.2+ with mutual TLS available for private deployments.
- Key rotation: CMKs follow your rotation policy; Redwood supports automated re-wrap workflows when you rotate keys and will re-encrypt stored objects using the new wrapped key on a scheduled maintenance window we coordinate.
- Audit/evidence: we can provide KMS grant logs, key access logs, and CloudTrail-style event exports under an evidence share agreement.

Open questions for FinBank: 
1) Do you need Redwood to store any plaintext key material (short answer: no, unless you request a custom flow; we strongly discourage).
2) Would you prefer the Hosted CMK grant pattern or full CloudHSM in your tenant?
3) Are there specific encryption standards/algorithms beyond AES-256 required?

Next steps I can take this week: fill the relevant sections of your PDF and share the technical note (attached). If helpful, we can schedule a 30-min call with our infra engineer to walk through the grant flow and CloudHSM integration.

Thanks,
